Pooled result

RR 1.105 (1.049 to 1.163), 95% interval

clinical cure at test-of-cure. random-effects, estimator REML, k = 3.

τ² 0 · I² 0% · Q 0.6562 on 2 df

The analysis population is part of the estimand and this pool crosses it. Read from the registrations on 2026-08-21: NCT00509106 registers 'Clinical Cure Rate for Ceftaroline Compared to That for Ceftriaxone at the Test of Cure (TOC) in the Modified ' (population: Mitte); NCT00621504 registers 'Clinical Cure Rate at Test-of-Cure (TOC) in the Modified Intent-to-Treat Efficacy (mitte) Populations' (population: Mitte); NCT01371838 registers 'Clinical Cure Rate for Ceftaroline Compared to That for Ceftriaxone at Test of Cure (TOC) in CE Population' (population: CE). The populations pooled are CE and mitte.

A clinically evaluable population excludes protocol violators and indeterminate responses, and microbiologically-defined populations exclude patients without a qualifying pathogen. Those are selected subsets of the modified intent-to-treat population and systematically yield higher cure rates. A cure-rate ratio computed in one is not an estimate of the same quantity as one computed in another, so this pooled value depends on which trial registered which population.

Not that the arithmetic is wrong. Not that the direction would reverse -- that would need the per-population counts and is not established. And not that these are non-inferiority trials: The registrations fetched do not use that word, so the design question is unresolved from the registry rather than assumed.

This screen found no published synthesis pooling these three trials. The nearest relevant record is a network meta-analysis across many community-acquired pneumonia regimens (PMID 34540732), which answers a different question from a ceftaroline-versus-ceftriaxone pool. 42 records matched, 42 read, 18 flagged by title, one appraised; the rest were not read, so absence here is absence from this screen and not from the literature.

Two contributing trials register the primary in the mitte population and one in the CE population. CE excludes protocol violators and indeterminate responses and systematically yields higher cure rates, so this ratio is assembled across quantities that are not the same quantity. GRADE indirectness is downgraded for it.

Unlike tigecycline, ceftaroline's result holds under adjustment: the Hartung-Knapp interval at k = 3 is 1.0356 to 1.1787 on t = 4.3027 with 2 df, and it still excludes no difference. Recorded because the two topics separate on exactly this.

Does the answer depend on the pooling method?

With two or three studies the Cochrane Handbook (10.10.4.4–10.10.4.5) asks for a sensitivity analysis comparing interval methods rather than a choice between them. Both are given here; the published interval is the first row.

Table 4. Does the answer depend on the pooling method?
IntervalMethodSummary (95% CI)
as publishedREML1.1048 (1.0494 to 1.1633)
sensitivity (Handbook 10.10.4.5)REML with Hartung-Knapp, t on k-1 = 2 degree(s) of freedom (t = 4.3027)1.1048 (0.9868 to 1.2371)

The published point is 1.1049 and the house-rule point is 1.1048. The number a reader remembers does not move; what differs is the precision claim. That is why nothing downstream catches this -- every memorable quantity survives.

A floor of 1 is applied to the variance-inflation factor so the adjustment can never narrow an interval below the unadjusted one. That guard is the recognised modification for exactly this instability, and its existence is evidence the small-k behaviour is a known problem with known handling rather than a novel judgement.

Introduction

Background. This review asks: In Ceftaroline fosamil versus ceftriaxone in bacterial pneumonia, what is the effect on versus intravenous ceftriaxone on clinical cure at test-of-cure? It pools 3 randomised trials, against intravenous ceftriaxone. The outcome pooled is clinical cure at test-of-cure. Every count and denominator behind those estimates is read as follows. Registry throughout. Every count and denominator read from ClinicalTrials.gov posted results.1

Sources for this section (1)
  1. manuscript.introduction

Methods — search

Primary trials. No bibliographic search for primary trials was run. The 3 included trials were identified by reading named registrations on 2026-08-18. All four seeded registrations read on 2026-08-18; three pooled, one excluded on the grounds stated in the analysis block. Published syntheses. PubMed E-utilities esearch + esummary, executed 2026-08-21. Query as executed: (ceftaroline[tiab]) and (pneumonia[tiab] or cabp[tiab] or cap[tiab]) and (meta-analysis[pt] OR "systematic review"[pt] OR meta-analysis[tiab] OR "pooled"[tiab] or focus[tiab]). It matched 42 record(s), of which 42 were retrieved and 42 read; 1 appraised.1

Sources for this section (1)
  1. bookkeeping_2026_08_21.the_search_its_date_and_its_databases

Methods — synthesis

For clinical cure at test-of-cure, a random-effects model was fitted with the REML estimator.1

Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 (Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials) , following . 3 result-level assessments were made.2

A ceiling applies to every risk-of-bias judgement in this review; it is stated with the assessment itself rather than summarised here.3

Certainty of evidence was rated with GRADE, following the Cochrane Handbook chapter 14. Randomised evidence starts HIGH and is rated down with reasons., following . 0 pooled outcome(s) were rated. No domain is rated UP; these are randomised trials starting HIGH. 1 outcome(s) were not rated because their pool is declined or withdrawn: there is no effect estimate to rate the certainty of, and rating one would be certainty about a number this review refused to publish.4

Results

The pooled risk ratio for clinical cure at test-of-cure was 1.1 (1.05 to 1.16) across 3 trials, against intravenous ceftriaxone.1

Noted on this pool. This screen found no published synthesis pooling these three trials. The nearest relevant record is a network meta-analysis across many community-acquired pneumonia regimens (PMID 34540732), which answers a different question from a ceftaroline-versus-ceftriaxone pool. 42 records matched, 42 read, 18 flagged by title, one appraised; the rest were not read, so absence here is absence from this screen and not from the literature. The analysis population is part of the estimand and this pool crosses it. Read from the registrations on 2026-08-21: NCT00509106 registers 'Clinical Cure Rate for Ceftaroline Compared to That for Ceftriaxone at the Test of Cure (TOC) in the Modified ' (population: Mitte); NCT00621504 registers 'Clinical Cure Rate at Test-of-Cure (TOC) in the Modified Intent-to-Treat Efficacy (mitte) Populations' (population: Mitte); NCT01371838 registers 'Clinical Cure Rate for Ceftaroline Compared to That for Ceftriaxone at Test of Cure (TOC) in CE Population' (population: CE). The populations pooled are CE and mitte. Two contributing trials register the primary in the mitte population and one in the CE population. CE excludes protocol violators and indeterminate responses and systematically yields higher cure rates, so this ratio is assembled across quantities that are not the same quantity. GRADE indirectness is downgraded for it. A clinically evaluable population excludes protocol violators and indeterminate responses, and microbiologically-defined populations exclude patients without a qualifying pathogen. Those are selected subsets of the modified intent-to-treat population and systematically yield higher cure rates. A cure-rate ratio computed in one is not an estimate of the same quantity as one computed in another, so this pooled value depends on which trial registered which population. Unlike tigecycline, ceftaroline's result holds under adjustment: the Hartung-Knapp interval at k = 3 is 1.0356 to 1.1787 on t = 4.3027 with 2 df, and it still excludes no difference. Recorded because the two topics separate on exactly this. Not that the arithmetic is wrong. Not that the direction would reverse -- that would need the per-population counts and is not established. And not that these are non-inferiority trials: The registrations fetched do not use that word, so the design question is unresolved from the registry rather than assumed.2

The trials' results were closely consistent with one another: I-squared, the share of the variation between them that is more than chance alone would produce, was 0%; the estimated variance of the true effects between trials (tau-squared) was 0, the heterogeneity test statistic Q was 0.656, on degrees of freedom 2.3

What this does not establish: Not that any trial is free of bias -- no risk-of-bias assessment is recorded, and a pooled estimate without one is arithmetic, not a graded finding. Not superiority: these are non-inferiority trials against an active comparator, and a risk ratio near 1 is the expected result of a successful one rather than evidence of equivalence. Not anything about the fourth seeded trial, which is excluded above. Not agreement with any published synthesis; none has been read.4

The full model output for every pooled outcome -- the call, the estimator, the heterogeneity statistics and the back-transformed interval -- is reproduced verbatim as Extended data at the end of this article, so every number above can be checked against the software that produced it.5

Certainty of the evidence

Certainty was rated with GRADE, following the Cochrane Handbook chapter 14. Randomised evidence starts HIGH and is rated down with reasons..1

No domain is rated UP; these are randomised trials starting HIGH.2

LOW certainty. Downgraded once for non-uniform masking with two unjudgeable domains, and once because the pool combines results defined in different analysis populations. Not downgraded for inconsistency or imprecision, neither of which the fit supports.3

clinical cure at test-of-cureLOW3HIGHrisk of bias -- All three results are some concerns: non-uniform masking (one trial's care provider unmasked) on an assessed cure endpoint, with deviations from the intended intervention and missing outcome data no information. (move: HIGH to MODERATE, down 1 level(s)); inconsistency -- The stored refit gives tau^2 exactly zero, Q 0.6553 on 2 df, p = 0.7206, I-squared 0.00%. The three trials agree. (move: no downgrade); indirectness -- the pool crosses an analysis-population boundary: two trials register the primary in mitte and one in CE. CE excludes protocol violators and indeterminate responses and systematically yields higher cure rates, so the pooled ratio is assembled across quantities that are not the same quantity. (move: MODERATE to LOW, down 1 level(s)); imprecision -- k = 3 and the effect is consistent. The Hartung-Knapp interval, 1.0356 to 1.1787 on t = 4.3027 with 2 df, still excludes no difference, so the conclusion survives the small-k adjustment. (move: no downgrade); publication bias -- k = 3; asymmetry tests have no power (Handbook 13.3.5.4). (move: Not assessable -- no rating applied)

Limitations

What this review does not give a clinician: the number of events in each arm, any absolute effect or number needed to treat and any measure of harm. A relative effect cannot be turned into the benefit or the risk facing one patient without them, so this review can support a judgement about what these trials found and not a judgement about what to do.1
